clue.text: Blunder in obscurity and suffering in utterance

indicators.note: in utterance means the words are spoken and we take what they sound like

parts.note: obscurity is MIST (fog that hides things) and suffering is ACHE, spoken together

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over their words while in a fog and in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a careless error, the same thing as a slip or gaffe.

clue.text: Is the child-bearing aristocrat a problem?

parts.note: the one who bears the child is the mother, MA
a lady is a titled noblewoman

explanation.surface: Asks whether a noblewoman having a baby causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is a problem afflicting someone, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Agree to form a colony

definitions.meaning: to agree on terms, as in settling a dispute
to make a new home in a place, as pioneers do

explanation.surface: Consent to found a new community abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling can mean reaching agreement, or establishing a colony in a new land.

clue.text: Novelist gets near, bent on …

indicators.note: the ellipsis runs this clue into the next, so the letters get into error, that is they are jumbled up

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer moves closer, determined on something left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on with '…' into 4 down, whose 'error' is what the letters NEARBENTON get into: they are scrambled to spell the novelist. 'bent' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest Brontë sister wrote Agnes Grey and The Tenant of Wildfell Hall, so she is a novelist.

clue.text: … 1 across, our leaderless enemy

indicators.note: leaderless means the word for the enemy loses its first letter

parts.note: terror, as in the war on terror, is the enemy we fight

explanation.surface: Our adversary, now without a chief, makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our' is a link pointing at terror as the common foe; 1 across is a mistake, and this answer is a synonym of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, the answer to 1 across, so the cross-reference gives a direct synonym.

clue.text: Claim of 11 1 across is probably this guy with half a bear

definitions.text: Claim of 11 1 across is probably this

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the bear's six letters are kept

parts.note: Rupert Bear is a much-loved British children's cartoon bear

explanation.surface: Someone claiming an intentional blunder is with a chap and half a teddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 1 across reads as DELIBERATE MISTAKE: claiming an error was deliberate often hides something. RUPERT Bear is a classic British comic-strip character, halved to RUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Claiming a blunder was intentional usually conceals the truth, which is a concealment or whitewash.

clue.text: Very many left when aristocrat comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the noblewoman encircles the letter for left

parts.note: a countess is a titled noblewoman

explanation.surface: A great number departed when a noblewoman pays a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Too many to count means a very large number, so the word works as innumerable.

clue.text: 5 across suggested for Ophelia

definitions.meaning: a cover-up, something that conceals, as a covering over the face does
Hamlet tells Ophelia 'Get thee to a nunnery', suggesting she take the nun's covering

explanation.surface: Something proposed for Shakespeare's tragic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the veil means to become a nun, which is what Hamlet urges on Ophelia.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil conceals, so it is a cover-up; and a nun takes the veil on entering a convent.

clue.text: Current study replacing first in Divinity

indicators.note: in means the new letter goes in place of the initial letter of the divinity subject

parts.note: divinity as a university subject is theology

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word replacing

explanation.surface: A modern subject swaps out the start of religious studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing first' gives R, the first letter of 'replacing', which takes the place of the T of THEOLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheology is the science of how materials flow, so it is a study of current in its sense of flow.

clue.text: False hats?

parts.note: rhyming slang for lies is the name of a round flat-topped hat style, so the hats are false statements

explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang 'porkies' (short for this phrase) are lies; it is also a style of hat with a flat crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is rhyming slang for lies, which are false, and also names a type of hat.

clue.text: Part of 14 take some translating

indicators.note: take some means use just a portion of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: A section of a language exercise takes a bit of translating.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is TONGUE, meaning a language, and this classical language is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of ancient Rome is one tongue among many, a part of the whole set of tongues.

clue.text: Regular guy heard on way home with organ

indicators.note: heard means the pieces are spoken and give the sound of the answer

parts.note: way is ROUTE, home is IN (at home), organ is EAR, spoken together

explanation.surface: A creature of habit listens on the way home while playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks to routine is a regular sort, a creature of habit.

clue.text: Consider on purpose

definitions.meaning: to weigh up or think over carefully

explanation.surface: Think it over, and do it intentionally.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to think carefully; as an adjective it means intentional.

clue.text: Hot soup, gentle if possible, said 1 across

indicators.note: possible suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks for hot soup, gently if possible, and gets it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken mistake is an accidental verbal slip, the 1 across being a mistake.

clue.text: Carrier with satisfactory genes?

definitions.meaning: a freight train carries goods, read as two words split differently
a good breed or lineage, the question mark flagging the respaced reading

explanation.surface: A bearer of good heredity.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way the letters are a freight train (GOODS TRAIN), another way a sound genetic line.
explanation.definitionFit: A freight train carries goods; a good strain is a healthy breeding line.

clue.text: See 12
Larder of traveller finding part of street paved with silver after cutback

indicators.note: after places the kerb and silver behind the reversed cut

parts.note: split into two words, the second telling us to spell the first in the opposite order
the kerb is the paved edge of the street
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A wanderer's food store is found on a silver-paved street after budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: An Australian word: tucker is food, and a swagman carried this bag of provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a swagman's food bag served as his larder on the road.

clue.text: Don't allow wood over head of string player

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
a joist is a wooden beam in the ceiling above you

explanation.surface: Forbid timber above a musician's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the banjo, a stringed instrument, is a string player.

clue.text: Familiar footballer keeping medal with nightwear

indicators.note: keeping means the footballer's nickname holds the medal inside it

parts.note: Becks is the familiar name of England footballer David Beckham
DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: A well-known footballer keeps his medal with his pyjamas.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks worn in bed are an item of nightwear.

clue.text: A month at dice is bad: you will have to be detoxed

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gambling at dice for a month is a bad habit needing a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Made free of germs and poisons, so cleaned up or detoxified.

clue.text: Buddhist tales feature in Muslim and Hindu homes

definitions.text: feature in Muslim and Hindu homes

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism
ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk

explanation.surface: Buddhist stories appear in homes of other faiths.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Asian households of both faiths, the zenana was the secluded women's quarters.

clue.text: Busy with brace in ship

indicators.note: in means the pair goes inside the vessel

parts.note: the ark is Noah's ship
a brace is a pair, two

explanation.surface: Occupied with a strut on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being occupied in one's job, at the office, means being busy.

clue.text: Good guy's setback with money in prison — 11 1 across?

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the prison

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person
read as set back, the word set written backwards
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A good man's reversal of fortune lands him in jail with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 1 across is DELIBERATE MISTAKE: the answer is what you might say after one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excusing a deliberate mistake might say they were only checking a response.

clue.text: Remove guys from country for model behaviour

parts.note: to deport is to remove someone, as the following words about a country confirm
men is a synonym of guys
the Model T was the famous Ford car, so T is a model

explanation.surface: Expel men from the nation for exemplary conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model behaviour' looks like the definition, but 'model' gives T (the Model T Ford); 'from country' completes the sense of Remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is the way a person carries and conducts themselves, their bearing or behaviour.

clue.text: Mountain dweller coming in without more ado

indicators.note: coming in means the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone arrives without further fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without more ado' looks like an idiom, but the letters sit inside 'more ado'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth an oread is a mountain nymph, so a dweller of the mountains.

clue.text: Relation may be related on the other side

indicators.note: related means told or narrated, so this is how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: an auntie is a family relation

explanation.surface: Kin may be connected through the other half of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means taking the opposing side.

clue.text: Old book (in English) with change of heart may be past praying for

indicators.note: change of heart means the middle letter is swapped for another

parts.note: beyond hope of cure, incurable

explanation.surface: An ancient English volume, altered at its centre, may be beyond saving.
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the heart of INCURABLE becomes N. '(in English)' tells you this is the English form of incunabulum, a book printed before 1501.
explanation.definitionFit: An incunable is a book printed very early, before 1501, so an old book.

clue.text: Massacre the way the doctor does it?

parts.note: à la is French for in the manner of
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A slaughter carried out in the manner a physician would do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo was the Texas mission where defenders were killed in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The fall of the Alamo mission in 1836 is remembered as a massacre of its defenders.

clue.text: See 21
Land where lions are on currency

parts.note: a den is a lair where lions live
the mark was a currency, for instance in Germany

explanation.surface: A country where big cats appear on the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian country, so a land.
